variables.policy_prompt_for_subgoal: Start in A: with the execution-start gripper empty, pick up the cube of the color named in the goal, pointing at its current visible center. Use only the execution scene for this pickup, not its earlier demonstration location. For every subgoal output, copy the menu label verbatim as the choice—'A', 'B', or 'C' for this menu—and supply any required [y, x] point separately. Never append the action description to the label. If the observed execution interval shows descent to that cube, closure to a grasp-sized opening (approximately 46%), and a lift with that opening maintained, choose B, dropping onto the goal-selected demonstration target stored in pre_press_target: the last completed target placement before the press for 'right before', or the first completed target placement after the press for 'right after'. Do not infer this temporal destination from the cube's current execution position. Explicit held-object evidence also permits B. The recorded cube coordinates may remain at the tabletop position after pickup and a held label may be absent; these do not override the closure-and-lift evidence. Match the remembered point to the corresponding visible target and point within that target, or use the remembered point if it is occluded. If pickup clearly closed on nothing or left the hand empty, choose A again at the requested cube. C is not required: the demonstration press identifies the desired target, and must not be reenacted. A completed release of the requested cube onto the selected target finishes the task; do not press the button afterward. For an otherwise unmatched nonterminal situation, choose B if there is credible evidence the requested cube is held, otherwise A at that cube. If pre_press_target is unknown and dropping is necessary, use the visible target nearest the requested cube as a deterministic fallback rather than asking for clarification.

fields.name: pre_press_target
fields.description: Despite its legacy name, this field holds the goal-selected demonstration target. When memory is empty and the demonstration is shown, locate the button press by closed-gripper descent onto the button and contact/depression, allowing temporary button occlusion. Read the temporal relation from the goal. For 'right before', find the instruction's cube's last completed target placement before the press. For 'right after', follow its next transfer and find its first completed target placement after the press; merely remaining on the old target immediately after button contact is not a new placement. Use release and subsequent resting evidence to identify the placement, allowing occlusion. Use the selected demonstration placement to identify the physical target, then follow that target through all subsequent demonstration frames to execution start, including shuffles, exchanges, crossings, and temporary occlusion. Resolve identity using the observed motion sequence and joint continuity of moving targets; do not assume spatial rank or target-list order identifies it, or independently match the final scene to its original position. Write exactly that physical target's reported execution-start center as [y, x], not its earlier demonstration center, the released cube's center, or the center of another target now occupying its former position. Ignore later placements when selecting the target, but continue tracking the selected target's subsequent motion. If its physical identity cannot be resolved, write "unknown". Once populated, copy the incoming value unchanged at every decision step; do not replace it with the cube's current position or a newly shifted visible centroid. If no target can be identified, write "unknown". e.g. [126, 145]
fields.annotation: Despite its legacy name, store the [y, x] center of the goal-selected demonstration target for the instruction's cube. Read the temporal relation from the goal: for 'right before', select the last completed target placement before the demonstration button press; for 'right after', select the first completed target placement after that press. Remaining on the old target immediately after button contact is not a new placement. Identify completed placements from release and subsequent resting evidence, allowing occlusion; do not substitute a later or final placement. Track the physical target selected by that placement through the entire remaining demonstration to execution start, including target shuffles, exchanges, crossings, occlusion, and small centroid shifts. Store exactly that physical target's reported execution-start center, not the center of whichever target occupies its former position. Resolve identity using the observed motion sequence and joint continuity of moving targets, not spatial rank, target-list order, or proximity to the original placement location. Later placements do not change which target was selected, but subsequent target motion must still be followed. If the selected physical target's identity cannot be resolved, write "unknown". Write this at decision step #1 and retain it unchanged thereafter. If the selected target cannot be identified, write "unknown". e.g. [126, 145]

fields.name: pre_press_target
fields.description: When memory is empty and the demonstration is shown, locate the button press by the closed gripper descending onto the button and its depression. Find the instruction's cube's last completed target placement before that event; if the cube is hidden during the press, use its preceding release and resting position. Match that target to the execution-start scene and write its visible center as [y, x]. Ignore subsequent cube placements when selecting the target. Once populated, copy the incoming value unchanged at every decision step; do not replace it with the cube's current position or a newly shifted visible centroid. If no target can be identified, write "unknown". e.g. [126, 145]
fields.annotation: Store the [y, x] center of the target on which the instruction's cube rested immediately before the demonstration button press. Identify it from the last completed placement before that press, not from later placements or the cube's final position. Use the selected target's center in the execution-start scene, matching it through the demonstration despite occlusion and small centroid shifts. Write this at decision step #1 and retain it unchanged thereafter. For episodes 7, 31, 47, 52, and 89 respectively, the values at both decision steps are [126, 145], [115, 152], [80, 162], [101, 163], and [76, 104]. e.g. [126, 145]

history.critique:
field pre_press_target, ANNOTATOR PROMPT
  A goal requested the target right after the demonstration press, but the annotation retained the before-press target; after pickup the policy consequently dropped toward the wrong target. This breaks SUFFICIENCY. Separately, a before-press goal was annotated with a target used only after the press, although the policy correctly extracted the earlier placement. This breaks PREDICTABILITY. Generalize this single field to hold the goal-selected demonstration target, retaining the existing field name for compatibility: for 'right before', select the last completed placement of the requested cube before the press; for 'right after', select its first completed target placement after the press, not the unchanged resting position immediately following button contact and not its final placement. Match the selected target through the demonstration to its execution-start center. Write that [y, x] at the first decision and retain it unchanged thereafter. For example, the after-press case must contain [86, 100], not [93, 162]. Correct the inconsistent before-press annotation to [76, 143], not [89, 165]. Do not create separate before and after fields or store the temporal relation already supplied by the goal. Remove episode-specific value prescriptions in favor of this general rule.

field pre_press_target, POLICY PROMPT
  When the goal asked for the target right after the press, the policy prompt extracted only the earlier placement, causing the subsequent drop to use that earlier target. This breaks SUFFICIENCY. In another demonstration the policy's before-press extraction disagreed with an annotation that incorrectly selected a later placement, breaking PREDICTABILITY; no additional historical field resolves that inconsistency. Define this existing field as the goal-selected target despite its legacy name. When incoming memory is empty and the demonstration is visible, identify the button press from closed-gripper descent at the button and contact/depression, allowing temporary button occlusion. Read the temporal relation from the goal. For 'right before', identify the requested cube's last completed target placement before the press; for 'right after', follow its next transfer and identify its first completed target placement after the press. Use release and subsequent resting evidence, allowing occlusion; merely remaining on the old target immediately after button contact is not a new placement. Match that target to the execution-start scene and write its center as [y, x], for example [86, 100] for an after-press selection. Ignore placements later than the selected event. Once populated, copy the value unchanged rather than recomputing from current cube or target centroids. Preserve 'unknown' only when the selected target cannot be identified. Remove the unconditional instruction to ignore all post-press placements.

the policy prompt for subgoal
  For an after-press goal, the requested cube had been picked up successfully, but the unconditional rule to drop onto the before-press target sent the policy to the earlier demonstration placement. The annotated memory contained only that earlier target, so SUFFICIENCY failed. Replace the description of B's destination with the goal-selected demonstration target stored in pre_press_target under its revised definition: last completed target placement before the press for 'right before', first completed target placement after the press for 'right after'. Match the remembered point to the corresponding visible target, or use the remembered point when occluded. Do not infer the temporal destination from the cube's current execution position. Preserve the pickup and closure-and-lift evidence rules, including their handling of stale cube coordinates and absent held labels. Preserve the rule that the demonstration button press is only a temporal reference and C must not be reenacted. A release onto the selected target completes the task. The inconsistent before-press recording must not motivate an exception that selects a post-press target: correct its annotation instead; its recorded later-target drop remains inconsistent with the goal and demonstration.

field pre_press_target, POLICY PROMPT
  At the initial decision for a goal requesting the target used right after the demonstration button press, the policy identified the correct target but wrote its early demonstration center [87, 93], whereas the annotated memory used its execution-start center [88, 94]. This is a PREDICTABILITY mismatch in coordinate selection, not a missing historical fact. Clarify the existing matching rule: use the demonstration placement to identify the target, then store exactly that target's reported center in the execution-start scene, rather than its earlier demonstration center or the released cube's center. The field still holds only the goal-selected target point, is initialized when the demonstration and execution-start scene are shown, and is copied unchanged thereafter. For example, write [88, 94] when that is the selected target's execution-start center. Retain the existing unknown fallback.

the policy prompt for subgoal
  At the initial decision, the goal requested placing the blue cube on the target used immediately after the demonstration press. The execution gripper was empty, and the policy correctly selected pickup at the visible blue cube, but emitted 'A pick up the cube' instead of the menu label 'A'. The annotated memory identified the selected post-press target using its execution-start center. This was an executable-output SUFFICIENCY failure, not a failure to identify the pickup object or temporal destination. Add an explicit output rule: the choice must be the menu label alone, copied verbatim—'A', 'B', or 'C' for this menu—with any required [y, x] point supplied separately. Never append the action description to the label. Retain the existing pickup, held-object, drop-destination, and no-button-reenactment rules.

After selecting the last completed placement before the press or first completed placement after it, track that target's identity through the entire remaining demonstration, including shuffles and crossings. If the observed execution interval shows descent to that cube, closure to a grasp-sized opening (approximately 46%), and a lift with that opening maintained, choose B, dropping onto the goal-selected demonstration target stored in pre_press_target: the last completed target placement before the press for 'right before', or the first completed target placement after the press for 'right after'. Do not infer this temporal destination from the cube's current execution position. Explicit held-object evidence also permits B. The recorded cube coordinates may remain at the tabletop position after pickup and a held label may be absent; these do not override the closure-and-lift evidence. Match the remembered point to the corresponding visible target and point within that target, or use the remembered point if it is occluded. If pickup clearly closed on nothing or left the hand empty, choose A again at the requested cube. C is not required: the demonstration press identifies the desired target, and must not be reenacted. A completed release of the requested cube onto the selected target finishes the task; do not press the button afterward. For an otherwise unmatched nonterminal situation, choose B if there is credible evidence the requested cube is held, otherwise A at that cube. If pre_press_target is unknown and dropping is necessary, use the visible target nearest the requested cube as a deterministic fallback rather than asking for clarification.

fields.name: pre_press_target
fields.description: Despite its legacy name, this field holds the goal-selected demonstration target. When memory is empty and the demonstration is shown, locate the button press by closed-gripper descent onto the button and contact/depression, allowing temporary button occlusion. Read the temporal relation from the goal. For 'right before', find the instruction's cube's last completed target placement before the press. For 'right after', follow its next transfer and find its first completed target placement after the press; merely remaining on the old target immediately after button contact is not a new placement. Use release and subsequent resting evidence to identify the placement, allowing occlusion. Use the selected demonstration placement to identify the target, then match that target to the execution-start scene. Write exactly that target's reported execution-start center as [y, x], not its earlier demonstration center or the released cube's center. Ignore placements later than the selected event. Once populated, copy the incoming value unchanged at every decision step; do not replace it with the cube's current position or a newly shifted visible centroid. If no target can be identified, write "unknown". e.g. [126, 145]
fields.annotation: Despite its legacy name, store the [y, x] center of the goal-selected demonstration target for the instruction's cube. Read the temporal relation from the goal: for 'right before', select the last completed target placement before the demonstration button press; for 'right after', select the first completed target placement after that press. Remaining on the old target immediately after button contact is not a new placement. Identify completed placements from release and subsequent resting evidence, allowing occlusion; do not substitute a later or final placement. Match the selected target through the demonstration to its center in the execution-start scene despite occlusion and small centroid shifts. Write this at decision step #1 and retain it unchanged thereafter. If the selected target cannot be identified, write "unknown". e.g. [126, 145]
